headline: Geopolitical Fog Hangs Over the Open as Hormuz Tensions and a Soft Dollar Set the Tone
body_html:
Monday's pre-market tone is cautious and event-driven. The dollar is pinned near multi-month lows as debt anxiety continues to weigh on investor sentiment, while gold has climbed to its highest level in more than three months as markets brace for upcoming U.S. inflation data. That combination — a weakening greenback and a flight-to-safety bid in bullion — suggests participants are hedging rather than pressing into risk heading into the week.

The dominant macro overhang is the Strait of Hormuz. Fewer than 20 vessels transited the strait over the weekend, a sharp drop in traffic that underscores the fragility of global energy logistics. Iran has issued warnings of fines and detention for ships it deems in violation of transit rules, while a reported cyber attack linked to Iran-affiliated actors has put British energy executives on alert. The U.S. is also preparing additional Iran sanctions, prompting China to signal it will defend its interests.

On the session just closed — Friday, August 21 — breadth within our universe was constructive, with 370 advancers against 175 decliners. Materials led all sectors, gaining 1.48%, while Semiconductors were the lone laggard at -0.23%. Watch for early pressure in energy-adjacent names and continued strength in defensive plays should Hormuz headlines intensify at the open.

briefs.headline: Gold Reaches Three-Month Peak Ahead of Inflation Reading
briefs.body: Bullion has advanced to its loftiest level since May as investors seek shelter ahead of closely watched U.S. inflation figures due later in the week. The move higher in gold coincides with broad dollar softness, with the greenback sitting near multi-month lows amid persistent concerns over the U.S. fiscal trajectory.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Traffic Falls Sharply Over Weekend
briefs.body: Shipping data shows fewer than 20 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, a notable decline that has refocused attention on the chokepoint's vulnerability. Analysts note that while crude volumes through the strait draw the headlines, a quieter but potentially more acute concern is a tightening supply of refined petroleum products in affected markets.

briefs.headline: Iran Warns Shipping; Oman Seeks Diplomatic Path
briefs.body: Tehran has put vessel operators on notice, threatening fines and detention for ships deemed to be violating Hormuz transit protocols. In a parallel diplomatic channel, Oman's foreign minister is set to travel to Tehran on Tuesday, signaling that Gulf mediators remain active in attempting to de-escalate maritime tensions.

briefs.headline: Cyber Incident Prompts UK to Brief Energy Sector Leadership
briefs.body: British officials convened energy industry executives over the weekend following reports of a cyber attack with suspected links to Iran-affiliated actors. The briefing reflects heightened concern that geopolitical tensions in the Gulf are beginning to manifest in infrastructure-targeting operations well beyond the immediate theater of conflict.

briefs.headline: U.S. Force Constraints Clip Joint Exercises With South Korea
briefs.body: Washington has canceled planned joint marine exercises with Seoul, citing constraints on military resources tied to the ongoing Iran situation. The decision underscores the extent to which the Iran standoff is reverberating across U.S. strategic commitments in Asia, adding a secondary layer of geopolitical uncertainty for markets to process.

briefs.headline: Materials and Alpha Metallurgical Headline Friday's Advancers
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources surged 8.09% to lead all gainers in Friday's session, helping push the Materials sector to a 1.48% gain — the best of any group tracked. Lithium name Albemarle added 6.75%, suggesting broad commodity enthusiasm, while Marvell Technology's 5.57% decline weighed on an already soft Semiconductors sector.
